corrections.form_value: construct usefulness, measure human_raters, and reported includes 'Length: Co-GPT M = 146.8, SD = 86.8 characters vs Self M = 97.7, SD = 50.7'
corrections.source_says: The length figures are character counts of the top-three representative post-its. They are not the groups' quality picks, and no rater produced them. The codebook classes length as elaboration (Section 6). Record them as a separate outcome (construct elaboration, question with_ai, unit output, p. 4, Section 4.2). Keep S1-O2 for the 9 vs 12 top-three picks and Table 1. The numbers are exact.
corrections.quote: The top three representative post-its from Co-GPT Ideation (M = 146.8, SD = 86.8) contained more characters than those in Self Ideation (M = 97.7, SD = 50.7).

confirmed: source.version is exact: the PDF on file is arXiv:2403.12928v1 [cs.HC], 19 Mar 2024, 8 pages (p. 1 margin stamp). The arXiv API lists v1 as the only version, with no journal reference or DOI. OpenAlex and Crossref show no published version (queried 6 October 2026).
Title and authors (Gionnieve Lim, Simon T. Perrault) match p. 1. Appendix A (pp. 7-8) holds Figures 3-6, one content-analysis figure per issue and phase, and no further statistics.

design_class quasi_people and context_class observational are correct. Every participant did Self Ideation first and Co-GPT Ideation second, in a fixed order (p. 5, Section 6, quote verbatim; p. 2, Section 3.1 and Figure 1). The only random step was forming groups of three (p. 2, Section 3.1). The paper does not say how groups got their issue.
No study randomly assigns people to generative-AI assistance, so has_randomized_people_study is false and criterion 1 is not_met.

People: 21 students (p. 3, Section 3.2, quote verbatim), in 7 groups, 4 on Misinformation and 3 on Hallucination (p. 3, Section 4). No exclusions are reported. The paper gives no head count per phase, but p. 1 (Section 1) says the 21 ideated alone and then with ChatGPT, which supports 21 analyzed in each arm. Criterion 2 is not_met (21 is below 50).

Units, not people: 108 Self Ideation post-its (Misinformation 70, Hallucination 38) and 119 Co-GPT Ideation post-its (70, 49). 59 prompts (36, 23) came from 17 conversations submitted voluntarily by the 21 participants (p. 3, Section 4).

participants.who matches p. 3, Section 3.2: 15 survey respondents, of whom 6 undergraduate, 6 master's, and 3 doctoral students. All participants had used ChatGPT before (p. 2, footnote 4). The model was ChatGPT v3.5 (p. 5, Section 6).
Task and timing match: both issue statements are quoted exactly (p. 2, Section 3.1). The two individual phases took 16 minutes and the workshop 40 minutes (p. 2, Figure 1 and Section 3.1).

S1-O1 reported string matches p. 3, Section 4.1: 23.6 percent more unique ideas (Self Ideation 38, Co-GPT Ideation 47), Misinformation 21 vs 26, Hallucination 17 vs 21. 47/38 = 1.2368, which would round to 23.7 percent. The form copies the printed 23.6 percent, as the rules require.

S1-O1 coding fits the source: post-its were clustered separately for each issue and phase (Appendix A, Figures 3-6), and an unclustered post-it counts as one unique idea (p. 3, Section 4.1). Construct diversity, question across_people, measure category_count, and unit set fit a count pooled over all participants' post-its.

S1-O2 counts match p. 4, Section 4.2 and Table 1: top-three post-its Self Ideation 9, Co-GPT Ideation 12, Misinformation 5 vs 7, Hallucination 4 vs 5. Table 1 First/Second/Third: Self 4/3/2, Co-GPT 3/4/5 (rows sum to 9 and 12).

S1-O2 quality is each group's own choice of its top three ideas, made with no explicit ranking metric (p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 4, Section 4.2). Post-its were colored so that author and phase could be told apart (p. 2, footnote 3). human_raters is the closest code, and criterion 3 is met through S1-O1 in any case.
The paper runs no statistical test: D1 used exploratory content analysis and D2 descriptive statistics (p. 3, Section 3.3).

one_line_finding numbers and locators are exact (47 vs 38, p. 3, Section 4.1; 12 vs 9, p. 4, Section 4.2 and Table 1). It does not mention that more Self Ideation post-its ranked first (4 vs 3, Table 1), which the paper uses to call the quality result not straightforward, but nothing in it contradicts the source.
No preregistration, company involvement, or data and code links are stated. An Institutional Review Board approved the study (p. 2, Section 3).

The blank fields (comparison_type, direction, statistics_available, timing, primary, diversity_detail) follow the short form for small experiments in tools/creativity-light.js, which leaves them at their defaults.
summary: The form is accurate on design, counts, version, and every printed number: 21 students brainstormed alone and then with ChatGPT in a fixed order, with no random assignment of AI, so the paper is quasi_people, observational context, not core, and has no study for the two-screener pipeline. One coding fix: the post-it length means (146.8 vs 97.7 characters, p. 4) are an elaboration outcome and should not sit inside the usefulness outcome S1-O2.
